title: High Row Machine
summary: A plate-loaded row that pulls down and back from overhead, a cross between a pulldown and a row.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.7 for upper back (helper): each working set adds 0.7 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.5 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Sit with your thighs under the pad and reach up for the handles.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your hips.
Let your arms go back up until your lats stretch.

form_cues.cue: Pull the handles down and back
Drive the elbows toward your hips
Drive the elbows, not the hands.

mistakes.text: Leaning back to use body weight.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Lat width focus, Steadier cable tension.
Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, One side at a time, Steadier cable tension.
